newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy business leaders back Fiat's Romiti.
newsitem.headline: Italy business leaders back Fiat's Romiti.

text.p: A group of 45 of Italy's top business figures on Thursday pledged their full support to Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti who last week received an 18-month suspended sentence for false accounting.

The group, including the honorary president of Italy's leading merchant bank Mediobanca, Enrico Cuccia, and other top industrialists, published a letter in Milan's financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore expressing support for Romiti.
The group included Antoine Bernheim, chairman of insurer Generali, and Montedison chairman Luigi Lucchini.

"The undersigned, who know the personal commitment, the moral rectitude and orthodoxy of behaviour that have always been a characteristic of Cesare Romiti's behaviour, want on this occasion to express all their respect and their full solidarity," the letter said.
On Wednesday, 5,000 of Fiat's managers and staff at Fiat's Turin headquarters also gave their support to Romiti at a meeting held in a former Fiat factory now converted into a conference centre.
Romiti's sentence was effectively suspended until the lengthy Italian judicial process is complete and Romiti may never serve the jail term.
Romiti is the the most prominent business figure to be convicted since Italy's so-called "clean hands" anti-corruption drive started in 1992. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
